Key risks: customer interest in VPC/private deployment, SOC2 audit timeline, and potential competition from Anthropic/OpenAI. Agreed to run technical deep dive and deliver pricing/benchmark details.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-18
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Marisol Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Partner Ops), Evan Brooks (Solstice Channel Director), Nada Hassan (Solstice Partner Manager), Tom Lee (Solstice Solutions Architect)

[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I think we have a full table, great to see the Solstice crew. Quick check, agenda is: run through the four joint opps, call out any blockers, tech asks, and confirm owners. Anything to add?

[00:18] Evan: No that sounds good. We want to make sure the top two deals are ready for exec outreach next week. Also, quick note, one of them is going through a procurement window in late Oct so timing's tight.

[00:33] Marisol: Cool, thanks. Marisol from the SE side — I can handle the deep dive on performance and sizing. I also want to flag that for the healthcare account we may need VPC or private deployment, possible on-prem discussion.

[00:48] Nada: Yup that's right. HIPAA-ish constraints, they'd prefer data not leave the region. They also asked about SOC 2 and audit history.

[00:56] Liam: Noted. We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO in our docs, I'll share the security pack, but for PII/HIPAA we'll likely recommend Redwood Private with customer-controlled VPC or our private endpoint. There's a short checklist we can send.

[01:12] Tom: Quick technical question — what's the deployment model for Private? Is it a managed box in their cloud account or full on-prem? They have EKS but limited GPU quota.

[01:25] Marisol: Good question. We support a few modes: customer-managed VPC where the control plane is private and they point to our runtime, or fully on-prem if required. For GPU constrained environments we can size a hybrid: dedicated instances for peak and hosted fallbacks. But we should validate concurrency and qps to pick instance types.

[01:44] Evan: For the healthcare target, expected concurrency is low, like 2-5 concurrent users, but peak inference QPS could spike to ~120 during batch windows.

[01:56] Marisol: That helps. For 120 qps with short seq lengths we can probably do a small dedicated pool; I'll run cost estimates.

[02:08] Liam: Ok, let's go through the pipeline doc — Priya, you shared the spreadsheet, right?

[02:15] Priya: Yep, I uploaded the shared co-sell pipeline at: https://redwood.app/partners/pipeline/solstice (note: short link in notes). The sheet lists the four accounts: Orion Health, Meridian Retail, Atlas Insights, and Cascade Insurance — prioritized by Solstice.

[02:30] Evan: Orion and Cascade are our focus. Cascade has procurement in late Oct, Orion is usually easier to get demos into.

[02:40] Liam: Great, let's start with Orion Health — status?

[02:45] Nada: Orion is in discovery. They care about latency for clinical decision support, and strict controls on PHI. They asked about model explainability and logs retention too.

[02:59] Marisol: For explainability we can instrument outputs with provenance metadata and provide traces to the customer. Logs retention is configurable; we have options to not persist full transcripts or to encrypt with customer KMS.

[03:15] Tom: The KMS question matters — customers insist on using their KMS. Do you integrate with AWS KMS or GCP KMS?

[03:23] Liam: Yes, we integrate with common KMS providers; we also support HSM integrations for enterprise. I'll include the security integrations doc in the follow-up.

[03:36] Evan: Good. Any blockers from your side on Orion?

[03:40] Nada: They want a quick benchmark — P50/P95 latencies, cost per 10k tokens — and a short demo with their clinical data mockups.

[03:50] Marisol: We can produce a benchmark. I want to propose two model options: a quantized open model for cost efficiency and a fully float model for higher accuracy. We'll show both tradeoffs in latency and token cost.

[04:05] Liam: Perfect — add that to action items. Next, Cascade Insurance — status?

[04:10] Evan: Cascade is paused until procurement, but we should be ready with pricing. They're comparing Redwood against Anthropic and some in-house options.

[04:20] Liam: Understood. For procurement we should prepare a comparison sheet: latency, cost, SLAs, and data controls. Also clear uplift for dedicated vs hosted pricing.

[04:33] Tom: On the in-house competitor — their infra might be cheaper but lacks observability and scaling. Can we quantify unit economics for the comparison?

[04:44] Marisol: Yes, we can. I can run a TCO-style slide showing tokens per dollar, ops burden reduction, and fallback reliability. That usually helps procurement decide.

[04:55] Evan: Great. For Atlas Insights and Meridian Retail — any quick notes?

[04:59] Nada: Atlas is a proof-of-concept lead; they want a short PoC with 6-week timeline. Meridian wants a demo and is price-sensitive.

[05:10] Liam: Ok, so priority order: Orion, Cascade, Atlas, Meridian. Any other risks?

[05:16] Tom: One small risk: Atlas is in EU, they require data residency. Do you have EU regions for Redwood Private?

[05:24] Priya: Yes we have EU deployments. For Private we can deploy into their preferred region or run our control plane in EU with customer-managed runtime. We'll outline options.

[05:36] Marisol: Also just flag model selection — some customers ask specifically for a model that supports function calling or structured output. We should confirm each customer's output requirements.

[05:48] Evan: Orion needs structured output for clinical coding, Cascade needs more free-form summarization.

[05:57] Liam: Good call — Marisol, include function-calling capabilities in the demo for Orion.

[06:05] Marisol: Will do. I'll prepare a demo harness and a short runbook for the PoC.

[06:12] Nada: On enforcement of roles: they want RBAC and SSO. Do you support Okta/SAML?

[06:19] Liam: Yes, SSO via SAML/Okta is supported. We'll include an onboarding checklist for SSO and RBAC mapping.

[06:28] Tom: Thanks. One more technical — if we go with dedicated GPU pools, what's the SLA on latency and failover?

[06:36] Marisol: Our Dedicated offering has configurable SLAs depending on commitment level. Typically 99.9% uptime with regional failover; we also support automatic fallback to hosted models when capacity is constrained, which reduces downtime. I'll attach SLA excerpts.

[06:50] Liam: Nice. Okay, let's lock owners: Marisol for technical deep dive with Tom, Liam for pricing and co-sell deck, Priya for GTM materials and partner tracking, Evan/Nada to confirm account contacts.

[07:05] Evan: We'll aim to have target contact lists by Tuesday. Also, we want a joint exec one-pager to take to the VP of Product at Cascade — can you tailor it to procurement concerns?

[07:18] Liam: Yes, we'll add procurement slide focusing on cost comparison, SLAs, and security controls.

[07:26] Nada: For the demo — can we get a recording of prior healthcare demo to reuse assets?

[07:32] Marisol: I have one, I'll share the recording and the demo script. Note: some names in the recording are redacted.

[07:40] (background: brief cross talk)

[07:45] Tom: Quick question on pricing model — is it strictly per-token plus reserved capacity, or do you offer blended pricing for pilots?

[07:54] Liam: We have flexible options. For pilots we often propose a short reserved capacity commitment with pilot discount or an accelerated usage tier. For larger deals we recommend reserved Dedicated with committed monthly throughput for predictability. I'll include sample numbers in the follow-up.

[08:09] Evan: Any references or case studies we can share for healthcare?

[08:14] Liam: I'll send 2 short case studies and a technical reference, plus the SOC 2 pack.

[08:20] Nada: Great. Timeline recap?

[08:23] Liam: Sure: immediate next - Liam sends deck + pricing + security docs (by Mon 9/20). Marisol schedules deep dive and shares demo assets (by Thu 9/24). Priya shares GTM cadence and tracking sheet (by Tue 9/21). Solstice to provide contact lists and account-level concurrency numbers (by Wed 9/22).

[08:43] Evan: Sounds good. Anything else?

[08:46] Nada: One more note — Cascade requested a compliance questionnaire for procurement. I'll forward their template to Liam after this call.

[08:56] Liam: Perfect, we'll fill that out. Thanks everyone. We'll sync next week same time unless we need to bump for deep dive.

[09:04] Tom: Thanks all.

[09:06] (call ends)

Notes and links referenced: https://redwood.app/security/soc2 (security pack), https://redwood.app/partners/pipeline/solstice (pipeline sheet), demo recording link (shared privately).

Transcript notes: transcription contains occasional mis-attributions and minor WER errors typical of automated transcription.
